sentenceSets.sentence: The company divested itself of subsidiaries that no longer aligned with its core strategy.

answerChoices.reasoning: Means to release or liberate, capturing some of divest's sense of removing something unwanted, though lacking the property/possession emphasis.
Means to get rid of or arrange, nearly synonymous with divest when describing removal of unwanted holdings.
Means to throw away or reject, very similar to divest in describing the act of getting rid of subsidiaries.
Means to cast off or remove, nearly identical to divest when describing the removal of business units.
Means to remove or exclude entirely, related to divest but emphasizes removal from operation rather than transfer of ownership.
Means to part or divide, related to divesting subsidiaries but doesn't emphasize the deprivation of ownership that divest implies.
Means to leave behind or forsake, related to divesting but suggests giving up rather than actively transferring ownership.
Means to convert to cash or dissolve, related to divesting but more specific about financial conversion than ownership transfer.
Means to keep or hold onto; directly opposite of divesting, since retained subsidiaries would still be part of the company.
Means to obtain or gain possession, opposite of divest, since acquiring subsidiaries adds to the company rather than removing them.
Means to grow or increase, opposite of the company's divestment strategy described in the sentence.

Means to deprive of possession or ownership, nearly identical to divest in describing loss of authority and position.
Means to free from duty or remove from position, capturing much of divest's sense though often used with gentler connotation.
Means to strip bare of covering or possessions, similar to divest in describing removal of all authority and rank.
Means to temporarily remove from office, related to divest but suggests temporary status rather than permanent deprivation.
Means to remove from employment or position, related to divest but less specific about deprivation of powers.
Means to remove from a position or seat of power, related to divest but focuses on position rather than deprivation of authority itself.
Means to release from duty or position, related to divest but emphasizes termination rather than active deprivation.
Means to advance to higher rank or status; directly opposite of the official being divested of authority and position.
Means to place in office or assign to position; opposite of removing and divesting authority from the corrupt official.
Means to forgive or exempt from punishment; the opposite action to divesting an official of authority as part of a settlement.

Means to forcibly take possession, similar to divest in describing removal of property from aristocratic ownership.
Means to assert ownership, related to the transfer of property but describes taking for self rather than specifically divesting from aristocracy.
Means to take officially for government use, related to divesting but emphasizes government use rather than redistribution to peasants.
Means to take by force for public use, related to divest but emphasizes forceful taking rather than deprivation of prior owners.
